_dates: Both dates are stated explicitly and are NEVER derived. A future import with
no config entry must fail rather than guess a date — the workbook's own
'Previous Week Update' column was measured to be an unreliable roll-forward:
of 42 rows matched by CAPP, 13 matched the tracker's current text, 22 matched
the tracker's PREVIOUS text (the column had been left stale a full cycle), and
7 matched nothing the tracker had ever held.
previous_report_date = 2026-09-04 is therefore an ASSIGNED date, confirmed by
the client, not an observed one. The reconciliation step records that
provenance on every row it proposes so it stays auditable and correctable.
_approved_new: Rows explicitly approved by the client for creation as new projects, keyed
by the exact cell they came from. Anything else that fails to match is
reported as unresolved and is NEVER created: an unmatched row is far more
often a matching failure than a genuinely new project.
